name: Epidemic Sound
tagline: Subscription music and SFX library with rights pre-cleared for use in videos, podcasts and streams.

pricing.basis: monthly per account, cheaper billed annually
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You are not paying for the player, the search box or the tidy mood filters. You are paying for a legal document: the right to put these specific recordings in monetized content without a copyright claim eating your revenue. An agent can clone the entire interface in an afternoon and it will be worthless, because the thing in the middle is tens of thousands of commissioned tracks that Epidemic owns outright plus the Content ID whitelisting pipeline that keeps YouTube off your back. The closest honest build is a library manager for music you already have the rights to, which solves organization, not licensing. If you want free music, the answer is a CC0 catalog, not a clone.
coreLoopDIY: Indexes a local folder of tracks you already licensed or CC0 downloads, extracts BPM, key, duration and loudness, and gives you a fast tag-and-search browser with per-use license receipts.
requirements: A folder of music you actually have rights to, or CC0 downloads
Optional: Jamendo or Free Music Archive API key for fetching CC-licensed tracks
whatYouLose: Pre-cleared commercial rights and the indemnification that comes with them
Content ID whitelisting, so random claims on your uploads become your problem
A curated catalog of tens of thousands of exclusive tracks plus stems and variants
Weekly new releases and a sound effects library you did not have to source
Plugins and direct import into Premiere, Final Cut and DaVinci
moatNotes: They commission and own masters outright, which is why they can grant blanket rights no aggregator can match.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a copyright claim on a video with 200,000 views costs more than a year of subscription, and because arguing with an automated claims system is a special kind of hell. Creators pay for the ability to stop thinking about it: pick a track, drop it in, publish, no dispute form. The catalog being decent is a bonus. The real product is the absence of risk, and risk is not something you can build in an empty folder.
notes: The browser is a weekend; the catalog and the clearances are not. The moat is owning the masters outright and a direct line into Content ID.
prompt:
Build a local-first music library manager for creators called "Crate". It organizes tracks I already have the legal right to use. It does not download, scrape or stream anything from commercial libraries.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript frontend
- Node 20 + Express backend in the same repo, run both with one `npm run dev`
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/crate.db
- ffmpeg and ffprobe shelled out for metadata, waveform and loudness
- No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics

Features, in scope:
1. Point the app at one or more local folders. Recursive scan for mp3, wav, flac, m4a. Store path, size, mtime. Re-scan is incremental.
2. For each track run ffprobe for duration, sample rate, channels, embedded tags (title, artist, album, genre). Run ffmpeg loudnorm analysis for integrated LUFS. Estimate BPM with a simple onset-interval autocorrelation in plain JS over decoded PCM, and label it "estimated" in the UI because it will sometimes be wrong.
3. Generate a 1000-point waveform peak array per track, cache it as JSON on disk.
4. Browser UI: virtualized table, instant filter-as-you-type over title/artist/tags, range filters for BPM, duration and LUFS. Click a row to play with an inline waveform scrubber using the Web Audio API.
5. Free-form tags plus a fixed mood vocabulary (calm, driving, tense, happy, dark, epic, playful). Multi-select tag edit on selected rows. Keyboard shortcuts for the common ones.
6. A "license" field per track: free text plus a file path to the receipt, invoice or license PDF I drop next to it. A track with no license shows a red dot. Add a filter for "unlicensed only" so I can see my own exposure.
7. "Use log": record that track X went into project Y on date Z. Export the log for one project as a markdown credits block, including whatever license text I stored.
8. Optional CC-licensed import: if JAMENDO_CLIENT_ID is present in .env, add a search panel that queries Jamendo, shows license type, and downloads a track into the library with its license URL prefilled. Skip the panel entirely when the key is absent.

Out of scope, do not build: any commercial catalog integration, any Content ID or claim handling, user auth, sync, mobile apps, stem separation, AI generation.

Secrets go in .env, loaded with dotenv, and .env is gitignored. Ship a README with install steps, the ffmpeg prerequisite, and a blunt paragraph stating this tool organizes rights you already hold and grants you nothing.
